issues.legal_issue: An adjudicating tribunal cannot dispose of a financial creditor’s insolvency application by directing settlement instead of deciding whether the application should be admitted or rejected on the applicable statutory criteria.
material_facts: Financial creditors filed an application seeking insolvency proceedings against a corporate debtor based on alleged non-payment of debt.
The debtor had settled with some creditors, but not all applicants; settlement discussions with others were still pending.
The adjudicating tribunal disposed of the application by directing the debtor to settle the remaining claims, without deciding the application on its statutory criteria.
The appellate tribunal upheld the disposition, and the Supreme Court set aside both orders and restored the application for fresh consideration.
issues.conclusion: The adjudicating tribunal could not compel settlement or dispose of the application on that basis. It had to decide whether to admit or reject the application under the applicable statutory criteria, so the application was restored for fresh consideration.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3(11), 3(12) and 7(1), (4), (5), (6) and (7) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the adjudicating tribunal must ascertain whether a default has occurred and then admit or reject the application according to the statutory conditions. Innoventive Industries Ltd. v. ICICI Bank explains that, once default is established, the application must be admitted unless it is incomplete or another statutory ground for rejection applies. The tribunal may encourage settlement, but as a creature of statute it cannot compel settlement or exercise an equitable jurisdiction outside the statutory framework; Pratap Technocrats (P) Ltd. v. Monitoring Committee of Reliance Infratel Limited and Arun Kumar Jagatramka v. Jindal Steel & Power Ltd. caution against such intervention.

predicates.financial_creditor_insolvency_proceeding: A financial creditor sought insolvency proceedings against a corporate debtor based on an alleged payment default.
predicates.settlement_used_instead_of_adjudication: The adjudicating tribunal disposed of the application by directing the debtor to settle claims rather than deciding the application.
predicates.statutory_criteria_unexamined: The adjudicating tribunal did not determine whether the application satisfied the applicable grounds for admission or rejection.

issues.definition: When a financial creditor seeks insolvency proceedings and the tribunal substitutes a settlement direction for deciding the applicable criteria, the application must instead be admitted or rejected on those criteria.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate tribunal cannot dismiss an appeal as not maintainable when the adjudicating tribunal failed to exercise its jurisdiction over an insolvency application.
material_facts: The adjudicating tribunal disposed of the financial creditors’ insolvency application by directing settlement instead of deciding it under the governing statutory criteria.
The appellate tribunal treated the matter as a pre-admission disposition and dismissed the appeal as not maintainable, although the settlement did not cover all applicants.
The Supreme Court held that the adjudicating tribunal had failed to exercise its entrusted jurisdiction and that a clear case for appellate intervention had been made out.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was maintainable, and the appellate tribunal erred in declining to exercise its jurisdiction. The Supreme Court set aside the appellate order along with the adjudicating tribunal’s order.
issues.legal_principle: Where an adjudicating tribunal fails to exercise jurisdiction entrusted to it over an insolvency application, an appellate tribunal cannot avoid review by characterizing the disposition as pre-admission or the appeal as not maintainable. The appellate tribunal must exercise its jurisdiction to address that failure. The Supreme Court applied the statutory limits on the adjudicating tribunal’s authority under Section 7(5) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

predicates.appeal_from_insolvency_application_dispo: A party appealed a tribunal’s disposition of an application seeking insolvency proceedings against a corporate debtor.
predicates.lower_tribunal_failed_to_exercise_jurisd: The adjudicating tribunal did not decide the application within the authority entrusted to it.
predicates.appellate_tribunal_declined_review_as_un: The appellate tribunal declined to review the disposition on the ground that the appeal was not maintainable.
predicates.appellate_tribunal_must_exercise_appella: The appellate tribunal exercises its jurisdiction to review the adjudicating tribunal’s failure to decide the application.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a tribunal’s failure to decide an insolvency application and the appellate tribunal declines review as not maintainable, the appellate tribunal must exercise its jurisdiction to review that failure.
